title: The retail returns replica: staff return fraud on copied bills, with the interview's traps planted
request: Phase 8, Part C (the owner): the owner's problem patterns 1 to 5 as test scenarios with planted traps: a rule computed with future data, duplicate bills split across train and test, and a drift period in the holdout.
plan: Invent a sales table (one row per bill, honest repeat purchases among them) and a returns table for forty stores over nine months.

Plant staff return fraud: a few dishonest cashiers issue a copy of a recent real bill (a new bill, the amount edited a little) or reuse one, and return it, mostly late in the evening, earlier and with new cashiers in the last three months.

Let the labels grow as the owner described: the late-evening rule first, then a team reviewing five returns a day (the rule's hits first, a random sample to fill the batch), and clustering around confirmed cases.
Prove with tests on three seeds that every trap bites and that no single column gives the fraud away, and keep the truth for tests only.

decisions.decision: A copy is a new bill in the sales table, a near-duplicate of a real one, not the real bill's identifier.
decisions.why: The owner's pattern says copies are rarely exact and are found by matching; reusing the identifier planted no near-duplicate at all (the review).

decisions.decision: The labels grow over time: the rule alone for the first four months, then the team's daily batch of five with its random part.
decisions.why: The owner's labels grew from rules to reviews; a daily batch with a random part gives the holdout reviewed labels to be judged on, and keeps the rule-only labels as the trap.

decisions.decision: Honest returns take any share of the bill and any refund method, honest bills are sometimes returned twice, and honest customers buy the same thing again.
decisions.why: The first version gave fakes a construction fingerprint (exact fractions, always cash) that solved them with no join; a test bed must not be solvable by an artefact.

decisions.decision: The written people for the journeys and a sealed set by an independent agent move to 30.11.
decisions.why: The journeys bring files through a problem kind's replica; this replica reaches the engine through the modifiers 30.11 builds, and the plan's 30.11 row now names them.

change: dclab_core/replicas/retail_returns.py (generate, save, the traps in its docstring; dclab-core 0.76.0); tests/test_retail_returns_replica.py (seven tests on seeds 0 to 2); the knowledge base gains the replica's example.

findings.defect: The copied-bills trap did not bite with three links.
findings.scenario: With only a bill returned twice, a bill from another store and a return by the selling cashier, fake returns were linked 54% of the time and honest ones 24%, under the test's margin.
findings.cause: Most copies are of a bill from the same store that nobody else returned: those three links miss them.
findings.fix: The links a careful data scientist builds include a cash refund on a card bill and an amount edited away from the bill's: fake returns are then linked 96% of the time against 30% for honest ones.

findings.defect: The review capacity did not bind.
findings.scenario: Forty reviews a day against about seventeen returns a day: every return could be reviewed, so precision at the capacity equalled the fraud rate for any score.
findings.cause: The capacity was set without counting the returns of a day.
findings.fix: Five reviews a day, fewer than the returns of almost every day; a test checks it binds.

findings.defect: The holdout had almost no reviewed labels.
findings.scenario: On one seed the last three months held no expert-confirmed fake, so the metric the facts prescribe was undefined.
findings.cause: Experts reviewed only rule-flagged returns, and the rule flags almost no fake after the drift.
findings.fix: The team's daily batch fills with a random sample of the day's other returns; a test asks for at least twelve reviewed fakes in the holdout.

findings.defect: The holdout did not line up with the drift and ended without fraud.
findings.scenario: Honest returns ran a month past the last day of fakes, so the last ninety days began before the drift and ended in a month no fake could fall in.
findings.cause: Returns were kept after the generator's last day.
findings.fix: The log ends with its last day; a test checks fakes reach the log's last week.

findings.scenario: A fake carried the real bill's exact identifier, so no near-duplicate existed and a split grouped by bill changed nothing.
findings.cause: The copy was modelled as a reference, not as a bill.
findings.fix: A copy is a new sales row with the same items, the amount edited within 5% and minutes after its original; tests check the copies and that some cross the time cut.

findings.defect: A construction fingerprint solved most fakes.
findings.scenario: Honest refunds were exact fractions of the bill and every fake was refunded in cash, so a simple score reached a near-perfect ranking with no join.
findings.cause: The honest and fake draws used different discrete values.
findings.fix: Honest shares are continuous, refund methods overlap, honest bills are returned twice; a test checks no returns column alone reaches 0.85 of ROC-AUC and that the cross-table link beats every single column.

findings.defect: Some returns happened before their sale.
findings.scenario: A return drawn on its sale day took an hour unrelated to the sale's, so dozens of honest returns preceded their bill.
findings.cause: The return's time was drawn as a day offset and an independent hour.
findings.fix: A return is its sale's time plus a positive delay, moved into the store's hours; a test checks every return follows its sale.

findings.defect: The tests were tuned to one seed or could not fail.
findings.scenario: Two checks failed on other seeds, one only re-read the generator's own choice of cashiers, and the link check passed on a single column.
findings.cause: The tests were written against seed 0 and compared the trap with itself.
findings.fix: Every check runs on three seeds; the future statistic is judged on the training period; new cashiers in the holdout are asserted; the join must beat the best single column.

findings.defect: The record's verdict was not grounded.
findings.scenario: The record said pass while one seed missed its own bar, and called a link definition fixed before the run when it was widened after.
findings.cause: The first record summarised instead of stating each seed against the bar.
findings.fix: The measurement states each seed's number and says which checks were revised after the first run.

findings.defect: One dishonest cashier crashed the generator.
findings.scenario: Generating with a single dishonest cashier raised an error: the early crew was empty.
findings.cause: Two thirds of one rounded down to none.
findings.fix: The early crew holds at least one cashier; a test generates with one.

measurements.name: the rebuilt replica's traps on seeds 0 to 2
measurements.gate: every trap bites on each of the three seeds: the review capacity binds, the holdout has at least twelve reviewed fakes, the rule judged on its labels gains over 0.1 of ROC-AUC, the future statistic gains over 0.03 on the training period, no returns column alone reaches 0.85 while the cross-table link beats every column, new cashiers start in the holdout, and the rule's recall falls by more than 0.5
measurements.result: fakes 157 of 5074, 177 of 5066 and 180 of 5055; the best single returns column at 0.74, 0.77 and 0.78 of ROC-AUC against the cross-table link at 0.84, 0.90 and 0.91; near-duplicate pairs 16985, 17206 and 17366 against 116, 147 and 159 copies; reviewed fakes in the holdout 22, 27 and 14
measurements.against_gate: Met on all three seeds after the rebuild; the bars were set by the review, after the first version's run, so this is a check of the design, not a blind measurement.
limits: Invented data: a score on it says whether DCLab's decisions are sound, never how a model would do on real returns.
Reviewed fakes in the holdout are as few as 14 on one seed: any holdout precision on them carries a wide interval.

outcome: A retail returns replica on which every trap of the interview bites a careless solution and no single column gives the fraud away, ready for the recipes to be certified on it.
lessons: A replica can be wrong by being too easy: check that no artefact of the generator solves it before checking that its traps bite.
A planted trap must be checked on several seeds, against the links a careful person would build.
risks: Not yet run through the engine: 30.11 certifies the modifiers on it and writes its journeys people and sealed set.
